Definition: An image wrapped onto a 3D surface, such as a photo of grass laid over the ground.
A description of how a surface looks: its texture pictures, and settings such as how shiny or bumpy it is. Quorum keeps each material in its own JSON file.
A group of images made to be used together for one material: a color map, plus maps for bumps, roughness, shadows in cracks and height.
A material made from just one image, with only color: no bumps or roughness.
The picture of a surface's colors, like a photo of it taken in flat, even light.
A picture that stores which way each tiny bit of a surface faces, so bumps and cracks catch the light even on a flat surface.
A picture that says which parts of a surface are rough and dull and which are smooth and shiny.
A picture that darkens the gaps and corners of a surface that light has trouble reaching.
A picture that says which parts of a surface stick up and which sink down. On terrain, it helps materials blend where they meet.
One material in a terrain's set of up to four. Painting decides where each layer shows.
A picture for one region of a terrain that records how much of each layer shows at each point, so you can paint grass in one place and rock in another.
How many meters of ground one copy of a texture covers before it repeats.
The rules the creator of a work sets for how other people may use it.
A license in which the creator gives up their rights, so anyone may use, change and share the work, even in something they sell, without asking.
Saying who made a work you used, and where it came from.
